name: KYC Verification Process
description: FirstUK Bank's Know Your Customer verification standard operating procedure governing identity and address verification requirements for customers. This process is owned by the Head of Compliance and applies across Compliance Staff, Branch Staff, and Operations teams. The SOP establishes mandatory KYC controls and verification gates before account activation.

name: Head of Compliance
description: Senior compliance leadership role responsible for ownership and governance of the KYC Verification SOP. This role has authority over the process design, implementation, and ongoing compliance oversight.

name: Compliance Staff
description: Compliance department personnel responsible for executing KYC verification procedures, document review, and compliance checkpoint validation as defined in this SOP.
context: Audience | Compliance Staff, Branch Staff, Operations

name: Branch Staff
description: Front-line branch personnel responsible for customer-facing KYC data collection, document gathering, and initial verification steps as part of the account opening workflow.
context: Audience | Compliance Staff, Branch Staff, Operations

name: Operations Staff
description: Operations team members responsible for system recording, data entry, and operational execution of KYC verification steps within the defined SOP.
context: Audience | Compliance Staff, Branch Staff, Operations

name: Know Your Customer Verification Process
description: End-to-end procedure for conducting KYC verification to confirm customer identity and address at account opening and periodically thereafter. The process ensures compliance with FCA COBS Part 10 and Money Laundering Regulations 2017.
context: Establish procedures for conducting Know Your Customer (KYC) verification to confirm customer identity and address at account opening and periodically thereafter
ensuring compliance with FCA COBS Part 10 and Money Laundering Regulations 2017

name: FCA COBS Part 10 Compliance Checkpoint
description: Mandatory regulatory compliance gate requiring adherence to FCA COBS Part 10 requirements for customer identity and address verification.
context: ensuring compliance with FCA COBS Part 10 and Money Laundering Regulations 2017

name: Money Laundering Regulations 2017 Compliance Checkpoint
description: Mandatory regulatory compliance gate requiring adherence to Money Laundering Regulations 2017 for customer due diligence and verification obligations.
context: ensuring compliance with FCA COBS Part 10 and Money Laundering Regulations 2017

name: Customer Identity Verification
description: KYC verification component focused on confirming customer identity as part of the account opening and periodic refresh process.
context: confirm customer identity and address at account opening and periodically thereafter

name: Customer Address Verification
description: KYC verification component focused on confirming customer address at account opening and periodically thereafter.
context: confirm customer identity and address at account opening and periodically thereafter

name: Account Opening Process
description: End-to-end procedure for opening new customer accounts across all channels (branch, online, postal). Applies to individual and joint account holders with periodic re-verification on a risk-based schedule.

name: New Customer
description: Individual applying to open a new account through any channel. Subject to identity and address verification requirements during account opening.

name: New Account
description: Account being opened for a new customer, subject to verification and compliance requirements across all delivery channels.

name: Joint Account Arrangement
description: Account held by two or more customers with shared rights and liabilities. Both joint account holders must complete identity and address verification independently.

name: Joint Account Holder
description: One of multiple customers holding rights and obligations over a joint account. Each joint holder must independently complete verification procedures.

name: Identity and Address Verification
description: Mandatory Know Your Customer process requiring verification of customer identity and address during account opening. Applied to all new customers and joint account holders on a risk-based periodic refresh schedule.

name: Know Your Customer Verification Process
description: End-to-end customer identity and address verification workflow executed over 1–2 business days. The process encompasses document collection, verification, address validation, risk assessment, system recording, and quality assurance, culminating in either KYC approval or escalation for failed verification.
context: ✅ KYC Complete & Approved or ❌ KYC Failed - Escalate

name: Document Collection
description: Initial step in which customer-provided information and supporting documents are collected as the foundation for KYC verification.

name: Document Verification
description: Validation and authenticity check of collected identification and supporting documents to confirm their legitimacy and completeness.

name: Address Verification
description: Verification of the customer's stated address against acceptable proof of address documentation to confirm current residence.

name: Risk Assessment
description: Evaluation of customer risk profile based on collected information, verified documents, and address details to determine compliance and onboarding suitability.

name: System Recording
description: Formal entry and storage of verified customer information, documents, and risk assessment outcomes into the bank's operational systems for audit and compliance purposes.

name: Quality Check
description: Final review and validation of all KYC steps, documentation, and system entries to ensure completeness, accuracy, and compliance before approval or escalation decision.

name: KYC Approval or Escalation Gate
description: Final branching point determining whether the customer's KYC verification is complete and approved, or whether the case must be escalated due to failed verification or unresolved issues.

name: Know Your Customer Verification
description: Compliance obligation requiring collection, verification, and recording of customer identity and address information. The process includes document verification, address validation, and risk assessment steps executed within 1–2 business days.

name: Document Collection Process
description: The initial step in customer identity verification where valid photo identification documents are requested and collected from the customer. The process specifies acceptable primary documents (UK Passport and UK Driving License) and establishes criteria for document validity, including expiry status, legibility, and security features.
context: Please provide a valid form of photo identification (UK Passport or Driving License)

name: Identity Document Request
description: The discrete action of requesting valid photo identification from the customer as the first step in the document collection process. The request specifies two acceptable document types: UK Passport or UK Driving License.
context: Please provide a valid form of photo identification (UK Passport or Driving License)

name: UK Passport Verification
description: UK Passport as an acceptable primary form of photo identification for customer identity verification. The document must be valid (not expired), with a clear photo page and all security features visible.

name: UK Driving License Verification
description: UK Driving License (photocard format only) as an acceptable primary form of photo identification for customer identity verification. The document must be valid (not expired), with visible signature and intact driving record.

name: Expired Document Rejection
description: Expired identification documents are explicitly unacceptable and must be rejected during the document collection process. This applies to all document types.

name: Damaged or Illegible Document Rejection
description: Damaged or illegible identification documents are explicitly unacceptable and must be rejected during the document collection process.

name: Provisional License Rejection
description: Provisional driving licenses are explicitly unacceptable as a form of photo identification and must be rejected during the document collection process.

name: Non-UK Document Verification
description: Non-UK identification documents are generally unacceptable unless verified via a secondary source, establishing a conditional acceptance pathway for foreign documents.
context: Non-UK documents (unless verified via secondary source)

name: Proof of Address Document Collection
description: The process of collecting acceptable documentary evidence of a customer's current address. Primary documents must be dated within 3 months and include utility bills, council tax documents, bank statements, or mortgage statements. Secondary documents include tenancy agreements, insurance policies, HMRC letters, and electoral register extracts.
context: Please provide a document confirming your current address

Acceptable Documents (Primary - Dated Within 3 Months): 1. Utility Bill (Gas, Electricity, Water, Telephone) 2. Council Tax Document (Bill or banding notice) 3. Bank Statement (Another bank's statement acceptable) 4. Mortgage Statement
Acceptable Documents (Secondary): Tenancy agreement (signed + landlord details), Insurance policy (buildings/contents), HM Revenue & Customs letter, Electoral register extract

name: Utility Bill
description: An acceptable primary proof of address document covering gas, electricity, water, or telephone services. Must be dated within 3 months of the address verification request.

name: Council Tax Document
description: An acceptable primary proof of address document issued by local authority, including either a council tax bill or banding notice. Must be dated within 3 months.
context: Council Tax Document (Bill or banding notice)

name: Bank Statement
description: An acceptable primary proof of address document from another financial institution. Must be dated within 3 months and confirm the customer's current address.

name: Mortgage Statement
description: An acceptable primary proof of address document issued by a mortgage lender. Must be dated within 3 months of the address verification request.

name: Tenancy Agreement
description: An acceptable secondary proof of address document. Must be signed and include landlord details to be valid for address verification purposes.

name: Insurance Policy
description: An acceptable secondary proof of address document covering either buildings or contents insurance. Confirms the customer's insured address.

name: HM Revenue & Customs Letter
description: An acceptable secondary proof of address document issued by HM Revenue & Customs confirming the customer's address for tax purposes.

name: Electoral Register Extract
description: An acceptable secondary proof of address document extracted from the electoral register confirming the customer's registered address.

name: Document Verification
description: A branch-based physical examination of original identity documents to verify authenticity, confirm customer identity through photo and signature comparison, check expiry status, and record document details for compliance purposes.

name: Original Document Examination
description: Physical inspection of the original identity document brought by the customer, including verification of authenticity through security features and watermarks, and confirmation that the document has not been tampered with.

name: Photo Comparison
description: Comparison of the photograph on the identity document to the customer's physical appearance to verify that the face matches and to note any discrepancies.
context: Compare photo on ID to customer's appearance

name: Signature Verification
description: Comparison of the signature on the identity document to the customer's signature on the application form to verify signature consistency.
context: Compare signature on ID to customer's signature on form

name: Expiry Check
description: Verification that the identity document has not expired and recording of the expiry date in the customer record.

name: Data Recording
description: Recording of document details including document type, document number, issue date, expiry date, and verification method into the customer record.
context: Record issue date and expiry date

name: Document Validity and Authenticity Gate
description: A branching gate that determines whether the document verification passes or fails based on expiry status, photo match, signature consistency, tampering, and security features. Pass leads to account opening continuation; fail results in rejection.
context: Pass Criteria: Document valid and not expired

name: Passport Verification
description: Passport document collected and verified during the document verification step, including authenticity checks, expiry verification, and photo/signature comparison.

name: Driving Licence Verification
description: Driving licence document collected and verified during the document verification step, including authenticity checks, expiry verification, and photo/signature comparison.

name: Branch Staff
description: Branch staff member responsible for conducting the physical document verification, including inspection of original documents, photo and signature comparison, expiry checks, and recording of document details.

name: Address Verification
description: A discrete verification step within KYC that examines address format compliance, matches addresses across identity and secondary documents, and validates document currency. The step applies pass/fail criteria based on address matching, UK residency confirmation, document recency, and postcode format validity.
context: Compare address on ID with address on secondary document
Utility bill, council tax: Dated within 3 months

name: Check Address Format
description: A sub-step within Address Verification that validates the format and location of the customer's address. Includes verification of UK postcode format compliance (A(1,2)9(1,2)A 9A(2)), confirmation of United Kingdom residency, and notation of any address concerns.
context: Confirm address is in United Kingdom

name: Match Address Documents
description: A sub-step within Address Verification that compares the address shown on the primary identity document with the address on a secondary supporting document. Investigates discrepancies such as recent moves or spelling variations.
context: Compare address on ID with address on secondary document
If addresses differ: Investigate (recent move? spelling variance?)

name: Document Currency Check
description: A sub-step within Address Verification that validates the recency and active status of secondary address documents. Applies different currency thresholds depending on document type: utility bills and council tax within 3 months, bank statements within 3 months, tenancy agreements must be signed and current, and insurance policies must be active.
context: Utility bill, council tax: Dated within 3 months
Tenancy agreement: Must be signed and current
Insurance policy: Must be active policy

name: Address Verification Pass/Fail Gate
description: A branching gate in the Address Verification step that determines whether the customer's address has met all compliance criteria. Pass outcomes require address matching across documents, UK residency, current secondary documentation, and valid postcode format. Fail outcomes are triggered by address mismatches, outdated documents, non-UK addresses, or invalid postcode format.
context: Pass Criteria: Address on ID matches secondary document

name: Primary Identity Document
description: The primary identity document presented by the customer during address verification, whose address is compared against secondary supporting documents as part of the KYC process.
context: Compare address on ID with address on secondary document
Address on ID matches secondary document

name: Secondary Address Document
description: A supporting document used to verify the customer's address during KYC. Acceptable document types include utility bills, council tax statements, bank statements, tenancy agreements, and insurance policies, each with specific currency and validity requirements.
context: Match Address Documents: Compare address on ID with address on secondary document
Utility bill, council tax: Dated within 3 months
Tenancy agreement: Must be signed and current

name: Customer Address
description: The customer's residential address subject to verification during the KYC process. Must be located in the United Kingdom, formatted with a valid UK postcode (A(1,2)9(1,2)A 9A(2)), and consistently recorded across identity and secondary documents.
context: Confirm address is in United Kingdom
Address on ID matches secondary document

name: Risk Assessment Process
description: A process to determine and categorize customer risk levels during account opening, classifying customers into Low, Medium, or High Risk categories based on nationality, residency, age, product type, deposit value, PEP status, adverse media, and AML jurisdiction controls.

name: Risk Category Determination
description: The step in which the responsible actor evaluates customer attributes against defined criteria to assign a risk classification (Low, Medium, or High).

name: Risk Category Gate
description: A branching decision point that classifies the customer into one of three risk categories (Low, Medium, or High) based on cumulative assessment of nationality, residency, age, product type, address jurisdiction, deposit value, PEP status, and adverse media findings.

name: PEP Screening Checkpoint
description: A mandatory compliance gate that verifies whether the customer is a Politically Exposed Person (PEP), with PEP status being a key factor in risk classification and a trigger for High Risk categorization.

name: Adverse Media Screening Checkpoint
description: A mandatory compliance gate that screens for adverse media including criminal history and fraud records, with findings triggering High Risk classification.

name: AML Jurisdiction Controls Checkpoint
description: A mandatory compliance gate that assesses whether the customer's country of residence or beneficial ownership jurisdiction has weak AML controls, which is a High Risk indicator.

name: SmartSaver Account
description: A standard banking product referenced as a Low Risk product type in the risk assessment framework.

name: Current Account
description: A standard banking product referenced as a Low Risk product type in the risk assessment framework.

name: UK National Customer
description: A customer classified as a UK national or long-term resident, which is a Low Risk indicator in the risk assessment process.

name: Non-UK Resident Customer
description: A customer who is a non-UK resident, classified as Medium Risk if from EU/developed country, or High Risk if from non-developed country with unclear beneficial ownership.

name: PEP Customer
description: A customer identified as a Politically Exposed Person, automatically classified as High Risk in the risk assessment framework.

name: UK Address Verification
description: Verification that the customer maintains a UK address, which is a Low Risk indicator in the risk assessment process.

name: Foreign Address Verification
description: Verification of a customer's foreign address, classified as Medium Risk if in EU/developed country or High Risk if in non-developed country.

name: Beneficial Ownership Screening
description: An AML screening step to verify clarity of beneficial ownership, with unclear beneficial ownership being a High Risk indicator.

name: Enhanced Due Diligence
description: Enhanced due diligence process triggered for high-risk customers, requiring additional verification of beneficial ownership and source of funds before account creation. Compliance Head approval is mandatory before proceeding.
context: Mark customer for Enhanced Due Diligence
Additional verification may be required (beneficial ownership, source of funds)
Compliance Head approval required before account creation

name: High-Risk Customer Classification Gate
description: Decision point that determines whether a customer is classified as high-risk, triggering escalation to Compliance Head and Enhanced Due Diligence requirements.
context: Mark customer for Enhanced Due Diligence

name: Mark Customer for Enhanced Due Diligence
description: Operational step to flag a high-risk customer for Enhanced Due Diligence review, initiating additional verification requirements.
context: Mark customer for Enhanced Due Diligence

name: Escalate to Compliance Head
description: Step to escalate high-risk customer cases to the Compliance Head for review and decision-making on account creation eligibility.

name: Beneficial Ownership Verification
description: Additional verification step required during Enhanced Due Diligence to confirm the beneficial ownership structure of high-risk customers.
context: Additional verification may be required (beneficial ownership, source of funds)

name: Source of Funds Verification
description: Additional verification step required during Enhanced Due Diligence to confirm the source of funds for high-risk customers.
context: Additional verification may be required (beneficial ownership, source of funds)

name: Compliance Head Approval for Account Creation
description: Mandatory approval step by the Compliance Head before account creation can proceed for high-risk customers undergoing Enhanced Due Diligence.
context: Compliance Head approval required before account creation

name: Compliance Head
description: Senior compliance role responsible for escalation review, approval of Enhanced Due Diligence findings, and authorization of account creation for high-risk customers.
context: Compliance Head approval required before account creation

name: High-Risk Customer
description: Customer classified as high-risk, subject to Enhanced Due Diligence requirements including beneficial ownership and source of funds verification before account creation.
context: Mark customer for Enhanced Due Diligence
Additional verification may be required (beneficial ownership, source of funds)

name: Beneficial Owner Identification Checkpoint
description: Mandatory compliance gate requiring verification and documentation of beneficial ownership for high-risk customers before account creation.
context: Additional verification may be required (beneficial ownership, source of funds)

name: Source of Funds Verification Checkpoint
description: Mandatory compliance gate requiring verification of the source of funds for high-risk customers as part of Enhanced Due Diligence.
context: Additional verification may be required (beneficial ownership, source of funds)

name: System Recording
description: A process step in which customer identity documents, address information, and risk assessment data are formally entered and recorded in the Account Management System (AMS). This step captures verification outcomes, document details, address records, and risk classifications for compliance and operational purposes.

name: Document Entry in AMS
description: The sub-step within System Recording where identity document details are entered into the AMS, including document type, number, issue date, expiry date, verification method, and verification status.

name: Address Entry in AMS
description: The sub-step within System Recording where customer address information is entered into the AMS, including address lines, city, postcode, country, address type classification, and supporting document type.
context: Document Type (Utility Bill / Council Tax / etc.)

name: Risk Assessment Entry in AMS
description: The sub-step within System Recording where customer risk classification is recorded in the AMS, including risk level assignment, Enhanced Due Diligence flag status, and the next scheduled review date based on risk-based scheduling.

name: Passport Verification
description: An accepted form of identity document collected and verified during the account opening process. Passport details including document number, issue date, and expiry date are recorded in the AMS.

name: Driving Licence Check
description: An accepted form of identity document collected and verified during the account opening process. Driving licence details including document number, issue date, and expiry date are recorded in the AMS.

name: Address Verification
description: The process of recording and verifying customer address information in the AMS, including address lines, city, postcode, country, and address type classification (Registered or Correspondence).

name: Proof of Address
description: Supporting documentation used to verify customer address, including utility bills, council tax documents, and other acceptable proof of address documents recorded in the AMS.
context: Document Type (Utility Bill / Council Tax / etc.)

name: Customer Risk Classification
description: A mandatory compliance gate where customer risk level is assessed and recorded in the AMS as Low, Medium, or High, with Enhanced Due Diligence flagging and scheduled review dates based on risk-based assessment protocols.

name: Enhanced Due Diligence Flag
description: A compliance control that flags customers requiring Enhanced Due Diligence based on risk assessment outcomes. The flag status (Yes/No) and reason are recorded in the AMS with a documented rationale.

name: Verification Method Recording
description: The recording of the method used to verify customer identity documents, including in-branch examination, online upload, or postal verification, along with the verification date and staff member identifier.
context: Verification Method (In-branch examination / Online upload / Postal)

name: Quality Check
description: A mandatory verification step performed before KYC approval that validates identity and address documents, confirms photo match, ensures all fields are recorded in AMS, completes risk assessment, and flags enhanced due diligence where applicable. The checklist is reviewed and signed off by Operations Manager or Compliance Staff before filing in the account record.
context: Manager Sign-Off: Operations Manager or Compliance Staff reviews checklist

name: Identity Document Collection and Verification
description: The step of collecting and verifying the customer's identity document in original or certified copy form as part of the KYC quality check.
context: Identity document collected and verified (original or certified copy)

name: Document Expiry Validation
description: Verification that the identity document has not expired as a mandatory check before KYC approval.

name: Address Document Collection
description: Collection of a current address document dated within 3 months as part of the KYC verification process.

name: Address Matching Verification
description: Verification that the address on the identity document matches the secondary address document to confirm consistency of customer information.

name: Photo Identity Verification
description: Verification that the photograph on the identity document matches the customer's appearance, either through direct visual comparison or certified match documentation.
context: Photo matches customer appearance (or certified match)

name: AMS Field Recording
description: Recording of all verified customer information and document details into the Account Management System (AMS) as part of the quality check process.

name: Risk Assessment Completion
description: Completion of the customer risk assessment as a mandatory step before KYC approval.

name: Enhanced Due Diligence Flagging
description: Flagging of enhanced due diligence requirements in the system when a customer is identified as high-risk during the quality check process.

name: Compliance Concerns Assessment
description: Assessment and documentation that no compliance concerns have been identified during the KYC quality check process.

name: Manager Sign-Off and Approval
description: Review and approval of the KYC quality check checklist by Operations Manager or Compliance Staff, with authority to approve or request additional verification before filing in the account record.
context: Manager Sign-Off: Operations Manager or Compliance Staff reviews checklist

name: Operations Manager
description: The role responsible for reviewing the KYC quality check checklist, approving or requesting additional verification, and filing the checklist in the account record.
context: Operations Manager or Compliance Staff reviews checklist

name: Compliance Staff
description: The role responsible for reviewing the KYC quality check checklist, approving or requesting additional verification, and filing the checklist in the account record.
context: Operations Manager or Compliance Staff reviews checklist

name: Identity Document
description: An official identity document required to be collected and verified in original or certified copy form, must not be expired, and must contain a photograph that matches the customer's appearance.
context: Identity document collected and verified (original or certified copy)
Photo matches customer appearance (or certified match)

name: Address Document
description: A current address document dated within 3 months that must be collected and verified to match the address on the identity document during KYC quality check.

name: KYC Approval Gate
description: A mandatory compliance checkpoint that verifies all KYC quality checks have been completed and approved before the account can proceed. The checklist must be filed in the account record as evidence of compliance.

name: KYC Verification
description: The Know Your Customer verification process that includes collection and verification of identity and address documents, photo matching, risk assessment, and compliance review before account approval.

name: Periodic Re-Verification Process
description: A risk-stratified Know Your Customer re-verification workflow that applies different verification schedules and monitoring intensities based on customer risk classification. The process includes automated reminders, ongoing risk assessments, and immediate re-verification triggers for compliance events.

name: Low-Risk Customer Re-Verification
description: Re-verification step for low-risk customers executed on a 5-year cycle with automatic system reminders. This step may be waived if customer activity demonstrates no increase in risk profile.
context: May be waived if customer activity indicates no risk increase

name: Medium-Risk Customer Re-Verification
description: Re-verification step for medium-risk customers executed on a 3-year cycle with quarterly risk assessments. Escalation is triggered if risk factors change during the monitoring period.

name: High-Risk Customer Re-Verification
description: Re-verification step for high-risk customers executed annually with quarterly enhanced monitoring and transaction-by-transaction review. Any risk changes trigger immediate escalation.

name: Immediate Re-Verification Trigger Assessment
description: Assessment step that evaluates whether immediate re-verification is required based on specific triggering events including address changes, disputes, fraud alerts, regulatory queries, PEP status changes, or sanctions list matches.

name: Risk Classification Gate
description: Decision point that routes customers into one of three re-verification schedules (Low-Risk, Medium-Risk, or High-Risk) based on their risk classification, determining the frequency and intensity of monitoring.

name: Immediate Re-Verification Trigger Check
description: Decision point that determines whether any of six triggering events (address change, dispute/complaint, fraud alert, regulatory query, PEP status change, or sanctions list hit) have occurred, requiring immediate re-verification outside the standard schedule.

name: System Reminder Generator
description: Automated system component responsible for generating and sending re-verification reminders to low-risk customers on their 5-year cycle.

name: Risk Assessment Reviewer
description: Role responsible for conducting quarterly risk assessments on medium-risk and high-risk customers and determining whether escalation is required based on risk factor changes.

name: Transaction Monitoring Analyst
description: Role responsible for conducting transaction-by-transaction review of high-risk customers to identify suspicious patterns and determine escalation requirements.

name: Risk Classification Checkpoint
description: Mandatory compliance gate that verifies customer risk classification is current and accurate before applying the appropriate re-verification schedule and monitoring intensity.

name: PEP Status Verification Checkpoint
description: Mandatory compliance gate that verifies PEP (Politically Exposed Person) status as part of the re-verification process, with PEP status changes triggering immediate re-verification.

name: Sanctions List Screening Checkpoint
description: Mandatory compliance gate that screens customers against sanctions lists during re-verification, with any sanctions list hit triggering immediate re-verification.

name: Periodic Customer Identity and Address Refresh
description: Ongoing Know Your Customer verification obligation that requires periodic re-verification of customer identity and address information on risk-based schedules ranging from annually (high-risk) to every 5 years (low-risk), with immediate re-verification triggered by specific compliance events.

name: Low-Risk Customer
description: Customer classification for individuals with low risk profile subject to re-verification every 5 years with automatic system reminders, unless customer activity indicates no risk increase.
context: May be waived if customer activity indicates no risk increase

name: Medium-Risk Customer
description: Customer classification for individuals with medium risk profile subject to re-verification every 3 years with quarterly risk assessments and escalation triggers for risk factor changes.

name: High-Risk Customer
description: Customer classification for individuals with high risk profile subject to annual re-verification with quarterly enhanced monitoring, transaction-by-transaction review, and immediate escalation for any risk changes.

name: Address Change Verification
description: Address verification event triggered when a customer registers a new address, requiring immediate re-verification outside the standard risk-based schedule.

name: Fraud Detection Alert
description: Fraud alert event that triggers immediate re-verification of the affected customer outside the standard risk-based schedule.

name: Ongoing Customer Monitoring
description: Continuous Anti-Money Laundering monitoring obligation applied to medium-risk and high-risk customers on quarterly cycles, with enhanced transaction monitoring for high-risk customers and escalation triggers for risk changes.

name: Re-Verification Process
description: A periodic re-verification procedure that mirrors the initial verification workflow. Customers are contacted to provide updated documents, which are then verified and recorded in the system with a re-verification date timestamp.

name: Customer Contact for Updated Documents
description: The step in which the customer is contacted and requested to provide updated identification and address documents as part of the re-verification process.

name: Document Verification and System Update
description: The step in which submitted documents are verified for authenticity and validity, and the customer's profile information is updated in the system accordingly.

name: Re-Verification Date Recording
description: The step in which the date of re-verification completion is formally recorded in the system for audit and compliance tracking purposes.

name: Re-Verification Identity and Address Verification
description: The periodic refresh of customer identity and address verification as part of the re-verification process, ensuring ongoing compliance with KYC obligations and maintaining current customer information.

name: Online KYC Verification
description: End-to-end digital Know Your Customer verification process for online account opening. Encompasses automated and manual document verification, address validation, and compliance approval gates. Timeline ranges from under 1 hour for straightforward cases to 1–2 business days when manual review is required.
context: If approved, account proceeds to AML screening
Timeline: <1 hour (if no issues), 1–2 business days (if manual review)

name: Document Upload
description: Customer uploads a photo of their identity document (Passport or Driving License) through the online portal. The system performs automated verification where available, followed by manual review by Compliance staff.
context: Customer uploads photo of ID (Passport or Driving License)

name: Document Verification
description: Compliance staff perform multi-point checks on the uploaded identity document: expiry date validation, document number format verification, image quality assessment, and flagging for manual escalation if clarity is insufficient.
context: Flag for manual review if unclear

name: Address Verification
description: Customer enters their address via online form. Automated postcode verification is performed, and an optional secondary document upload is available if required. Compliance staff review the address data before approval.

name: Compliance Approval Decision
description: Compliance staff make a final approval or rejection decision. Approved applications proceed to AML screening. Rejected applications trigger customer notification without disclosure of regulatory reasons.
context: Compliance staff approves or requests clarification
If approved, account proceeds to AML screening
If rejected, customer notified (not a regulatory reason disclosed)

name: Compliance Staff
description: Compliance team members responsible for manual review of uploaded identity documents, address verification, and final approval or rejection decisions in the online KYC process.
context: Compliance staff approves or requests clarification

name: Automated Verification System
description: Automated system that performs initial document verification checks and postcode validation where available, before escalation to manual Compliance staff review.

name: Document Clarity Assessment
description: Decision gate determining whether the uploaded document image quality is sufficient for verification. Unclear images are flagged for manual escalation; clear images proceed to format and expiry checks.
context: Flag for manual review if unclear

name: Compliance Approval Gate
description: Final compliance decision point where Compliance staff approve the KYC verification and allow the account to proceed to AML screening, or reject the application and notify the customer.
context: Compliance staff approves or requests clarification
If approved, account proceeds to AML screening

name: KYC Verification Checkpoint
description: Mandatory regulatory compliance gate verifying that customer identity and address have been properly collected, verified, and documented before account activation. Completion is required before AML screening can proceed.
context: If approved, account proceeds to AML screening

name: Passport Verification
description: Passport document accepted as valid identity proof in the online KYC process. Subject to expiry date check, document number format verification, and image quality assessment.
context: Customer uploads photo of ID (Passport or Driving License)

name: Driving License Verification
description: Driving License document accepted as valid identity proof in the online KYC process. Subject to expiry date check, document number format verification, and image quality assessment.
context: Customer uploads photo of ID (Passport or Driving License)

name: Address Verification Step
description: Customer-entered address subject to automated postcode verification and optional secondary document upload. Compliance staff review the address data as part of the KYC verification process.

name: Online Account Applicant
description: Individual applying to open an account online who must complete KYC verification by uploading identity documents and providing address information.

name: Identity and Address Verification
description: Comprehensive Know Your Customer process combining identity document verification (Passport or Driving License) and address validation through automated postcode checks and optional secondary documentation.

name: Postal KYC Verification
description: A Know Your Customer verification process conducted via postal submission of certified identity and address documents. The customer provides notarized copies of ID and proof of address, which are verified by a solicitor or notary public, then reviewed and recorded by bank operations staff. The process is designed to complete within 3–5 business days.
context: Certified copy of ID (notarized by solicitor, notary public)

name: Customer Document Submission
description: The customer provides certified copies of identity and address documents to initiate the postal KYC verification process. Both documents must be notarized by a solicitor or notary public.
context: Certified copy of ID (notarized by solicitor, notary public)

name: Solicitor/Notary Certification
description: A solicitor or notary public verifies the customer's identity, confirms the authenticity of the documents, and provides formal certification by stamping and signing the copies with a certification date.

name: Bank Certification Review
description: Operations staff review the certified documents, confirm the certifier's details (notary or solicitor), and may contact the certifier to verify authenticity if concerns arise. The outcome is recorded in the bank's system.
context: May contact certifier to verify (if concerns)

name: Solicitor/Notary Public
description: An external professional (solicitor or notary public) responsible for verifying the customer's identity, confirming document authenticity, and providing formal certification through stamping and signing.
context: Certified copy of ID (notarized by solicitor, notary public)

name: Operations Staff
description: Bank staff responsible for reviewing certified documents, validating certifier credentials, contacting certifiers if verification concerns arise, and recording the verification outcome in the bank's system.
context: May contact certifier to verify (if concerns)

name: Certified Copy of Identity Document
description: An official identity document (such as a passport or driving licence) provided as a certified copy, notarized by a solicitor or notary public to verify its authenticity as part of the postal KYC process.
context: Certified copy of ID (notarized by solicitor, notary public)

name: Certified Copy of Address Document
description: An official proof of address document provided as a certified copy, notarized by a solicitor or notary public to verify the customer's residential address as part of the postal KYC verification process.

name: Identity Verification
description: The verification of the customer's identity through review of a certified identity document by both a solicitor/notary and bank operations staff, confirming the document's authenticity and the customer's identity.
context: Certified copy of ID (notarized by solicitor, notary public)

name: Address Verification
description: The verification of the customer's address through review of a certified address document by both a solicitor/notary and bank operations staff, confirming the document's authenticity and the customer's residential address.

name: Customer
description: The individual applying for or undergoing postal KYC verification, responsible for providing certified copies of identity and address documents to the bank.
context: Certified copy of ID (notarized by solicitor, notary public)

name: Escalation and Exception Handling Process
description: A process that defines when and how to escalate customer verification failures and compliance exceptions to the Compliance Head. Covers scenarios including unacceptable identification, address mismatches, document fraud indicators, identity uncertainty, high-risk customer flags, and customer refusal to provide verification.
context: Customer unable to provide acceptable ID

name: Escalation Decision Trigger Assessment
description: The step where operational staff evaluate whether a customer verification scenario meets one or more escalation criteria and determines if escalation to Compliance Head is required.
context: Customer unable to provide acceptable ID

name: Escalation to Compliance Head
description: The action of escalating a flagged customer verification case to the Compliance Head for review and decision when exception criteria are met.

name: Operations Staff
description: The frontline operational role responsible for identifying verification exceptions and determining whether escalation criteria have been met during customer onboarding or verification processes.
context: Customer unable to provide acceptable ID

name: Compliance Head
description: The senior compliance authority responsible for reviewing and making final decisions on escalated customer verification exceptions, including cases involving unacceptable identification, address mismatches, document fraud, high-risk customers, and verification refusals.
context: Customer unable to provide acceptable ID

name: Acceptable Identification Provided
description: A gate determining whether the customer has provided identification documents that meet acceptable standards. Failure triggers escalation to Compliance Head.
context: Customer unable to provide acceptable ID

name: Address Verification Match
description: A gate determining whether the customer's provided address matches verification records. Mismatch flags possible fraud and triggers escalation to Compliance Head.

name: Document Authenticity Check
description: A gate determining whether identification documents appear genuine and unaltered. Detection of forgery or tampering triggers escalation to Compliance Head.

name: Customer Identity Clarity
description: A gate determining whether the customer's identity is sufficiently clear and unambiguous from provided documentation. Unclear identity triggers escalation to Compliance Head.

name: High-Risk Customer Classification
description: A gate determining whether the customer is classified as high-risk, including PEP (Politically Exposed Person) status or adverse media findings. High-risk classification triggers escalation to Compliance Head.

name: Customer Verification Cooperation
description: A gate determining whether the customer cooperates and provides required verification documentation. Customer refusal to provide verification triggers escalation to Compliance Head.

name: Acceptable Identification Compliance Gate
description: A mandatory compliance gate verifying that the customer has provided identification documents meeting regulatory and policy standards before proceeding with account opening or verification.
context: Customer unable to provide acceptable ID

name: Address Verification Compliance Gate
description: A mandatory compliance gate verifying that the customer's provided address matches verification records and does not indicate fraud before proceeding with account opening.

name: Document Authenticity Compliance Gate
description: A mandatory compliance gate verifying that identification documents are genuine and unaltered before accepting them as valid verification evidence.

name: PEP and Adverse Media Screening Compliance Gate
description: A mandatory compliance gate verifying that the customer has been screened for PEP status and adverse media findings before proceeding with account opening.

name: Acceptable Identification Document
description: Official identity documentation that meets the bank's standards for customer verification. The document must be provided by the customer and verified as acceptable during the onboarding process.
context: Customer unable to provide acceptable ID

name: Address Verification
description: The process of verifying that a customer's provided address matches records held by the bank or verification service. Address mismatches flag potential fraud and trigger escalation.

name: PEP Screening
description: Anti-Money Laundering screening to identify whether a customer is classified as a Politically Exposed Person (PEP), which triggers high-risk classification and escalation to Compliance Head.

name: Adverse Media Screening
description: Anti-Money Laundering screening to identify adverse media findings associated with a customer, which triggers high-risk classification and escalation to Compliance Head.

name: Customer Identity Verification
description: The Know Your Customer process of verifying that a customer's identity is clear and unambiguous through acceptable identification documents. Unclear identity triggers escalation to Compliance Head.

name: Exception Process
description: An end-to-end procedure for handling exceptions during account application workflows. The process requires documentation of the exception reason, escalation to the Compliance Head for review and decision, and system recording of the outcome. Three decision paths are available: approval with conditions, request for alternative verification, or rejection.

name: Document Exception Reason
description: The initial step in the exception process where the reason for the exception is formally documented. This creates the record that will be escalated for compliance review.

name: Escalate to Compliance Head
description: The documented exception is escalated to the Compliance Head for formal review and decision-making. This step transfers ownership from the initial documenting role to senior compliance authority.

name: Compliance Head Exception Review and Decision
description: The Compliance Head reviews the documented exception and makes a binding decision on how to proceed. Three distinct outcomes are possible: approval with additional conditions, request for alternative verification, or rejection of the account application.

name: Record Decision in System
description: The Compliance Head's decision and rationale are formally recorded in the system. This creates an audit trail and ensures the decision is available for future reference and compliance reporting.

name: Compliance Head Exception Decision Gate
description: A three-way decision gate where the Compliance Head determines the outcome of the exception review. The decision branches into approval with conditions, request for alternative verification, or rejection of the account application.

name: Compliance Head
description: The senior compliance authority responsible for reviewing documented exceptions and making binding decisions on account applications. The Compliance Head has authority to approve with conditions, request alternative verification, or reject applications.

name: Exception Documenting Officer
description: The role responsible for documenting the reason for an exception in the initial step of the exception process. This role prepares the exception record for escalation to the Compliance Head.

name: Staff Training and Competency Program
description: A mandatory staff training and certification program covering document authentication, customer communication, system data entry, and compliance procedures. Staff must pass a knowledge assessment, complete practical observation on 5+ customers verified by a manager, and complete annual refresher training to maintain certification.
context: Staff Required Training: Document authentication (spotting fakes, security features), Customer communication (explaining KYC requirements clearly), System data entry (accurate recording), Compliance procedures (what to escalate)
Practical observation (verified by manager on 5+ customers)

name: Document Authentication Training
description: Training module covering document authentication techniques, including spotting fake documents and identifying security features. This is a required component of the staff competency program.

name: Customer Communication Training
description: Training module focused on customer communication skills, specifically on explaining KYC requirements clearly to customers. This is a required component of the staff competency program.

name: System Data Entry Training
description: Training module covering accurate system data entry procedures. This is a required component of the staff competency program.

name: Compliance Procedures Training
description: Training module covering compliance procedures and escalation protocols. This is a required component of the staff competency program.

name: Knowledge Assessment
description: A mandatory knowledge assessment that staff must pass as part of the certification requirement for the training and competency program.

name: Practical Observation Verification
description: Practical observation verification conducted by a manager on a minimum of 5+ customers to validate staff competency in applying training to real-world scenarios.
context: Practical observation (verified by manager on 5+ customers)

name: Annual Refresher Training
description: Annual refresher training required to maintain staff certification and competency in all training modules.

name: Branch Staff
description: Branch staff members who are required to complete the training and competency program, including document authentication, customer communication, system data entry, and compliance procedures.

name: Manager
description: Manager responsible for verifying practical observation of staff on 5+ customers as part of the certification requirement.
context: Practical observation (verified by manager on 5+ customers)

name: KYC Requirements Communication
description: Staff training component focused on clearly explaining KYC requirements to customers as part of the broader training and competency program.

name: Policy Customer Identification
description: Detailed KYC policy document that defines customer identification requirements and procedures. Referenced as the authoritative source for Know Your Customer verification obligations.

name: Policy AML
description: Anti-Money Laundering policy document that defines screening procedures and requirements. Follows KYC verification in the customer onboarding workflow.

name: Account Opening Process
description: End-to-end account opening procedure that includes KYC verification as Step 3. Defines the workflow for establishing new customer accounts.

name: Business Ontology
description: Reference document defining Customer and Identification Document entities used across banking operations. Provides canonical definitions for data model consistency.
